chunks: And with the former chain of narration from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Habib al-Sajistani, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, peace be upon them both,
who said: It is written in the Torah, among what Allah, Most High, confided to Musa, peace be upon him, that He said to him: O Musa,

fear Me in your private affairs, and I will guard your secrets; and remember Me in your solitude and in the moments of your pleasures, and I will remember you during your lapses; and control your anger against those over whom I gave you authority, and I will withhold My anger from you;

and conceal the hidden treasure of My secret in your inner self, and show prudent concealment on My behalf in the presence of My enemy and your enemy among My creation; and do not invite abuse against Me from them by revealing the hidden treasure of My secret, lest you become a partner with My enemy and your enemy in cursing Me.

key_terms.التَّوْرَاةِ: The Torah, the scripture revealed to Prophet Musa (AS)
key_terms.الْمُدَارَاةَ: Prudent concealment, tactful dealing with adversaries — a key concept related to taqiyya
key_terms.نَاجَى: To confide in secret, intimate discourse (munajat) between God and His prophet

ai.seo_question: What did Allah say to Prophet Musa in the Torah about fearing God in private and controlling anger?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) transmits a divine address from the Torah in which Allah instructs Prophet Musa (AS) on the reciprocal covenant of private devotion. Each divine command carries a corresponding divine reward: fear God in secret and He guards your weaknesses; remember Him and He remembers you; restrain anger and He restrains His wrath. The teaching culminates in the obligation of taqiyya — concealing sacred knowledge from enemies to protect God's honor, a principle that held particular resonance for the early Shia community living under hostile authorities.
